title: Park unrooted DNS filtering; keep the WireGuard client setup and the firewall fix
objective: Stop pursuing phone-side DNS filtering until an always-on resolver exists. Android's Private DNS fails closed, so a resolver hosted on a machine that can be switched off leaves the phone with no internet at all - which is disqualifying for a daily driver. Success is: config.sh reverted so deploying is byte-identical to before, the phone left on working DNS, the reasoning and the ruled-out options recorded, and the working artifacts (WireGuard client setup, nftables scoping) kept rather than discarded.
acceptance_criteria: DNS_TRUSTED_DOT_HOST and DNS_TRUSTED_DOT_IPS are empty, and the enforcer harness confirms an empty allowlist plus Private-DNS-forced-off, i.e. the pre-change behaviour
The phone is left at private_dns_mode=off with DNS resolving
The fail-closed behaviour is recorded as measured on-device, not inferred
setup_dot_resolver.sh permits 853 on wg0 only - the input chain is policy drop and previously admitted only ssh over the tunnel, so binding to the tunnel address was not by itself sufficient
setup_phone_wireguard.sh installs, pushes and verifies the tunnel, and deletes the pushed private key afterwards
The parked doc names the specific reasons the hosted-hybrid option was ruled out, so it is not re-proposed
out_of_scope: Signing up for any DNS provider
Tearing down the local stunnel DoT endpoint - it is WireGuard-only and unreachable from LAN and WAN, so it is left running for future testing
Any Device Owner provisioning or factory reset
verifier: The stubbed-iptables harness (14 checks, section A proves the revert); shellcheck + shfmt on both scripts; setup_phone_wireguard.sh --check; adb settings get global private_dns_mode plus a ping from the phone
